cross_market_insights: The SERP is commercial and navigational in every market: planner homepages, lead directories (WeddingWire, Junebug, WedMeGood, Hitched), the local pack and Facebook or Reddit threads. No market shows an independent, criteria-led guide on choosing a planner in Italy in its top 3.

The same Facebook group thread ranks in Sydney, Dubai, Riyadh, Qatar and Hong Kong, and Reddit ranks in NY, Singapore and the Sydney informational SERP. Couples are crowdsourcing recommendations from strangers: the trust gap is the opportunity.

Australia: the only Australian-specific results are planners who straddle both countries (Lario, Lake Como and Australia; Instagram planners based Perth-Rome and Australia-Italy). Australians clearly value someone who bridges the time zone, but no page explains how to plan with an Italian planner from Australia.

US: Junebug's directory and a NY-based agency lead; the AI Overview pushes legal-vs-symbolic and cites US Embassy guidance. PAA is US-centric ('Can Americans legally marry in Italy?') and even appears in Gulf SERPs. Nothing addresses Australian legal recognition.

Gulf (Dubai, Riyadh, Qatar): results are generic international planner sites and directories; nothing addresses Arab or Muslim ceremonies, multi-day Lebanese or Gulf celebrations or Arabic-speaking teams. A secondary gap where Wedded Wonderland's cultural fluency is a differentiator.

India (Mumbai): PAA asks 'How much does it cost to hire a wedding planner in Italy?' and 'Can an Indian citizen get married in Italy?'; large multi-day weddings imply production-scale planners. Fee questions recur across markets.

Fees are the most repeated unanswered question (related searches 'wedding planner italy cost' in AU, SG, HK; PAA in Dubai, Riyadh, Qatar, Mumbai). Ranking pages either hide fees ('on request') or quote package numbers with no scope. Nobody explains flat fee vs percentage vs supplier commissions, or who the planner works for.

Service-level confusion: a Singapore-ranked thread asks about day-of coordinators vs planners; truewedstory is the only page separating planner, coordinator and designer. Nobody adds the venue's in-house coordinator or an advisory or matchmaking layer.

Informational competitors are thin or self-interested: elleffevents (800 words, Dec 2023, generic tips on a planner's own blog); Italian Wedding Designer (long question list answered from one agency's side); truewedstory (photographer's shortlist with half the content on photography). None tell the reader how to judge a planner's answers.
Nobody covers what a paying parent needs: how deposits and EUR payments flow, contracts in Italian or English, who is physically on site on the day, wet-weather and heat plans, older guests.
Our own site already ranks for nothing in these SERPs (no weddedwonderland.com URL in any top 10 checked).
payload.recommended_angle: The Australian couple's guide to choosing (and checking) an Italian wedding planner: which kind of planner your wedding actually needs, how Italian planners charge and who they really work for, the questions that separate a good planner from a polished Instagram, and how it works from the other side of the world. Wedded Wonderland Concierge is positioned honestly as the independent advisory layer that helps you decide whether you need a planner and, if so, matches you with a vetted partner, not as a planner itself.
